note: The long sleeps between books (none between Chicago and New York). from and to are book ids; growth multiplies his fortune (before orders and steward); village is how much Collesanto grows; events are the history the sleep passes through, each adding risk. investments are orders tied to one gap ($ do sleep_invest): growth multiplies, risk adds danger, humanity is lost on waking, flag notes what a later book reads. A gap marked split is one segment of a longer sleep played by interlude chapters, and is skipped by quick start (which uses the whole gap, listed first, instead). Segments with the same chain add up in the wake report: wake("years") and wake_event() cover the whole chain. rome_to_florence is the whole Lost Centuries sleep for quick starts; its four segments are what Book One plays: rome_to_sack (chapter 20), sack_to_byzantium, byzantium_to_plague and plague_to_florence (the interludes). Years and growth of the segments add up to the whole gap.
